facts.topic: A response close packet cannot close an active client container
facts.contract: The matched client handler branches on mServerInitiatedClose. When it is false and the local player has a live nonnull container manager, the handler sends PacketViolationWarning with severity Warning(0), violation type Unknown(-1), violating packet ID PacketViolationWarning(156), and the exact context below. It leaves the container manager open. No received container ID or type equality test occurs in this response branch.
facts.context: Server sent a ContainerClosePacket response packet when it should have sent the server initiated packet

facts.topic: A response received after the manager has closed finalizes the screen stack
facts.contract: When mServerInitiatedClose is false but no live container manager exists, the handler calls ItemStackNetManagerBase::onContainerScreenClose. It does not reconstruct or open a manager and does not send the warning. The recovered handler does not match a pending response by the incoming container ID or type. The screen-stack close helper preserves the base screen, as separately established in item_prediction_reconciliation_findings.json.

facts.topic: Server-initiated close schedules type-matched screen closure
facts.contract: A true server-initiated close with a live manager records its container type and should-close flag in LocalPlayer::ContainerCloseInfo. The normal ContainerScreenController tick closes only when its manager type equals that pending type and mScreenCanBeClosedByServer is true. A true server close without a live manager is ignored. The handler does not use the incoming container ID to select which manager closes. A separate option-dependent immediate deletion branch exists; it is not generalized here to every UI mode.

facts.topic: Actual manager deletion sends the ordinary close response then clears the manager
facts.contract: LocalPlayer::deleteContainerManager first flushes pending stack requests. If the current container manager is live, it obtains that manager container ID and sends ContainerClose with that ID, container type None(-9), and serverInitiatedClose=false. It then clears the player container manager. This same deletion routine is used for ordinary client closing and the recovered server-triggered deletion path; it does not echo the incoming server container type or ID blindly. Exact UI scheduling and every event subscriber remain outside this contract.
